english.title: Aggravated vehicle taking - ( driver did not take ) and vehicle damage of £5000 or over
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), knowing that a mechanically propelled vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), had been taken without the consent of the owner or other lawful authority, drove the said vehicle, and after the vehicle was unlawfully taken and before it was recovered, damage was caused to the vehicle.

(A)_[There were no other additional aggravating factors]_
(B)_[Additional aggravating factors were **(..SPECIFY THE FACTORS..)]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 12A of the Theft Act 1968.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Mandatory drug test required if 18 or over
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This wording is for use ONLY were the defendant was a 'SUBSEQUENT DRIVER' - for the 'initial taker' see H4381 and 'being carried on' see H4487.
(ii) See also H4392, H4385, H4386, H4387, H4483 and H4485 for other aggravated vehicle taking wordings relating to a 'subsequent driver'.
(iii) This offence wording should ONLY BE USED for damage five thousand pounds or OVER or where value initially unknown.
(iv) See offence wordings: H4485 for damage UNDER five thousand pounds.
